subject: SigmaCloud - GCP private offer commit phasing (staircase proposal)
messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason@sigmacloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.procure@sigmacloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer sizing + redemption cadence

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is our usage projection for the next 12 months (Sigma_ProjectedUsage_Jul-Aug.xlsx). We're serious about moving to a committed private offer on GCP, but procurement needs a tighter redemption cadence than the flat monthly amortization we discussed. Specifically: can Redwood support a "staircase" redemption where the bulk of the commit is available in the first 90 days to support our launch spike, then steps down?

Questions from my side:
- Any constraints on frontloading (first 30–90 days) from Redwood or GCP marketplace?
- How would invoicing and credits look if we frontload consumption?
- SLA guarantees during the initial ramp (we run customer-facing features at launch)

Sarah (cc'd) is our procurement lead — they'll need a proposal we can take to legal. Attaching the projection for context.

Thanks,
Jason
Head of Platform — SigmaCloud
[jason@sigmacloud.com]

Attachment: Sigma_ProjectedUsage_Jul-Aug.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason@sigmacloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer sizing + redemption cadence

Jason / Sarah —

Appreciate the projection — gives us a clean runway to propose a phased commit that matches your launch profile. Summary of what Redwood can do on the GCP private offer side:

1) Staircase redemption (recommended):
   - Phase A (day 0–90): 50% of committed credits available for redemption to cover launch spike
   - Phase B (day 91–180): additional 30% becomes available
   - Phase C (day 181–365): remaining 20%

2) Invoicing and credits:
   - We can invoice per milestone (Phase A invoice at activation, Phase B/C invoiced when phase unlocks) or amortize across 12 months — happy to align to what procurement prefers.
   - Co-sell credit can be applied as a one-time rebate at Phase A activation to help offset launch costs.

3) SLA / capacity:
   - We will reserve dedicated capacity for the first 90 days in us-central1 with a canary buffer to handle your initial spikes. SLA for dedicated pools is available as part of the Dedicated offering; private-offer-backed reservations come with a 99.5% uptime target for the reserved capacity.

Next steps I suggest:
- I’ll attach a redlined MOU (Redwood_PrivateOffer_v3.pdf) showing the staircase language and invoice triggers.
- If procurement prefers DocuSign, I'll generate an envelope for the Phase A terms while we finalize detailed SOW.

I’m looping in Sergio from Partnerships and Ben from Finance to align billing cadence and marketplace mechanics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_v3.pdf (offer draft), commit-staircase-MOU.docx (word stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer sizing + redemption cadence

Marissa / Sergio —

Quick finance note on invoicing: if we do milestone invoices tied to phase unlocks we need to confirm how GCP marketplace will route those invoices back to Redwood vs. to Sigma (this affects revenue recognition). Naomi, can you weigh in on:

- Preferred invoice cadence from Redwood's perspective (milestone vs flat amortization)
- Any constraints on applying one-time co-sell credits during Phase A without delaying recognition

Assuming Sigma frontloads a significant portion (50%), we should also propose a simple reconciliation mechanism at month 3 to true-up consumption vs committed credits.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Revenue Ops
ben@redwood.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer sizing + redemption cadence

Ben / Marissa —

Finance perspective: milestone invoicing tied to phase unlocks is workable but requires clear triggering events that are visible to both Redwood and GCP billing:

- Phase A trigger = activation + committed capacity reservation in GCP (we should include resource IDs in the MOU).
- Phase B/C triggers = calendar-based unlocks (day 91, day 181) or consumption thresholds (e.g., 80% of Phase A consumed). Either approach works; consumption thresholds add reconciliation overhead but align incentives.

Co-sell credits: we can apply as an offset at Phase A invoice provided the credit is documented and the rebate is paid within the same fiscal quarter — otherwise recognition gets hairy.

Action items for the MOU:
- Add explicit invoice routing (bill-to entity and billing email).
- Include a 30-day reconciliation window after each phase unlock for any usage true-up.
- Insert a clause for reserved capacity IDs and a short-run canary buffer (region: us-central1).

I’ll draft the billing appendix and loop back.

- Naomi
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

From: Jason Liu <jason@sigmacloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.procure@sigmacloud.com>, marketplace-sales@gcp-partners.google.com
Date: 2026-08-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer sizing + redemption cadence

Marissa / team —

Thanks — this looks reasonable and aligns with our launch window. A couple quick asks before we route to legal:

1) Can you produce a DocuSign envelope for Phase A only (activation + reserved capacity) so we can approve the frontload immediately and get the marketplace offer live?
2) Please confirm the canary buffer size (min vCPU / GPU pool) that you will reserve in us-central1 to ensure we don’t hit throttling during the first 30 days.
3) Legal will want to see a short note on termination rights if reserved capacity is not available for more than 72 hours within a 30-day window.

If you can send the Phase A DocuSign and the draft billing appendix (including invoice routing and the 30-day reconciliation window) we’ll start signatures on Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to get this live.

Jason
Head of Platform — SigmaCloud
[jason@sigmacloud.com]
